The Python equivalent of Mongoose in 2026 is Beanie — an async ODM built on Motor + Pydantic. It fits naturally into FastAPI (which is also Pydantic-based) and gives type-safe models, async I/O, validation, indexes, hooks, links (relations), aggregations, and migrations in one package. This post covers the working set: models, CRUD, indexes, links + back-links, hooks, projections, aggregations, transactions, integration patterns with FastAPI.
Series map: 17 base course → 18 Mongoose deep → 19 Beanie + FastAPI (this post) → 20 Outbox → ... → 29 K8s + mongosync + cost.

# main.py
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI
from motor.motor_asyncio import AsyncIOMotorClient
from beanie import init_beanie
from .models import User, Order, Product
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
client = AsyncIOMotorClient(os.environ["MONGO_URI"], maxPoolSize=50, appName="shop-api")
await init_beanie(database=client.shop, document_models=[User, Order, Product])
yield
client.close()
app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
init_beanie registers your models against the database and creates declared indexes. One call per process.

# models.py
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Annotated, Optional
from beanie import Document, Indexed, before_event, Replace, Insert
from pydantic import BaseModel, EmailStr, Field
class Address(BaseModel):
city: str
country: str = "UK"
class User(Document):
name: str
email: Annotated[EmailStr, Indexed(unique=True)]
age: Optional[int] = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=150)
role: str = "user"
tags: list[str] = []
address: Optional[Address] = None
created_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=datetime.utcnow)
class Settings:
name = "users" # collection name
use_state_management = True # for Save / Replace
indexes = [
"created_at",
[("name", 1), ("created_at", -1)], # compound
]
@before_event(Insert)
async def normalise(self):
self.email = self.email.lower()
Key elements:
Inherit Document. _id auto-managed as ObjectId.
Annotated[Type, Indexed(...)] for index declarations.
Settings inner class for collection name + index definitions.
@before_event / @after_event hooks similar to Mongoose middleware.
Pydantic v2 validators (Field(ge=0)) run on construction + assignment.

# create
u = User(name="Ada", email="ada@x")
await u.insert()
# read
u = await User.get(some_id)
u = await User.find_one(User.email == "ada@x")
users = await User.find(User.age > 25).sort(-User.created_at).limit(20).to_list()
# update
u.age = 31
await u.save()
# or atomic via update operators
await User.find_one(User.email == "ada@x").update({"$inc": {"login_count": 1}})
# delete
await u.delete()
await User.find(User.role == "user", User.age < 18).delete()
Query expressions use the Python operators on model fields — fully type-checked.

class Product(Document):
name: str
price: Annotated[float, Indexed()]
category: Annotated[str, Indexed()]
class Settings:
indexes = [
[("category", 1), ("price", 1)], # compound
IndexModel([("name", "text")], default_language="english"), # text
IndexModel([("location", "2dsphere")]), # geo
]
Indexes created at init_beanie. For production, disable + create via migrations (same advice as Mongoose Post 18).

Beanie supports linked documents — equivalent to Mongoose populate:
from beanie import Document, Link
class User(Document):
name: str
class Order(Document):
user: Link[User] # stored as { id, collection }
total: float
# Insert
ada = User(name="Ada"); await ada.insert()
o = Order(user=ada, total=99); await o.insert()
# Fetch with link
o = await Order.get(order_id, fetch_links=True)
print(o.user.name) # populated
# or one at a time
await o.fetch_link(Order.user)
Multi-level fetch supported. Like Mongoose populate, this issues additional queries — for hot endpoints prefer aggregation $lookup.
BackLink[T] for reverse references (also fetched on demand).

class UserProjection(BaseModel):
name: str
email: str
users = await User.find().project(UserProjection).to_list()
# Returns UserProjection instances (slim), not full User docs
Use for list endpoints — server returns only projected fields + Pydantic constructs the typed slim object.

result = await User.aggregate([
{"$match": {"role": "user"}},
{"$group": {"_id": "$country", "count": {"$sum": 1}}},
{"$sort": {"count": -1}},
]).to_list()
Returns raw dicts. To get typed results, pass a projection_model:
class CountryCount(BaseModel):
country_id: str = Field(alias="_id")
count: int
result = await User.aggregate(
[...],
projection_model=CountryCount,
).to_list()
For aggregation builders + type-safe pipeline construction, the community pyodmongo and helpers exist. Most teams just use dict pipelines as in mongosh.

from beanie import Transaction
async with await client.start_session() as session:
async with session.start_transaction():
await User.find_one(User.id == 1, session=session).update({"$inc": {"balance": -100}}, session=session)
await User.find_one(User.id == 2, session=session).update({"$inc": {"balance": 100}}, session=session)
Or with retry helper from Motor (Post 09 patterns apply).
session= must be passed to every op — same rule as Mongoose + the official driver.

from beanie import BulkWriter
async with BulkWriter() as bulk:
await User(name="A").insert(bulk_writer=bulk)
await User(name="B").insert(bulk_writer=bulk)
await User.find_one(User.name == "A").update({"$set": {"role": "admin"}}, bulk_writer=bulk)
# committed on exit
Batches the operations into a single bulkWrite call — much faster than per-doc round-trips.

Beanie has beanie migrate CLI:
beanie new-migration --name add_email_index
# edit the generated python file with up() / down()
beanie migrate -uri "mongodb://..." -db shop
Migration files apply schema-evolution + index changes idempotently. State stored in migrations_log collection.
For complex schema versioning (Post 07), pair with _schema_v on documents + lazy migration in app code.

Pitfall · Cause · Fix
init_beanie called per request · overhead, leak risk · call once in lifespan
Links populate causing N+1 · many docs each fetch_links · aggregation $lookup
Projection model field name mismatch · aliases needed · use Field(alias="_id")
EmailStr install error · missing optional dep · pip install pydantic[email]
Auto-index blocks on production startup · huge collection · disable + migrate manually
Mixed sync + async code · accidental blocking call · wrap with asyncio.to_thread
Old Pydantic v1 examples · breaking changes · always use Pydantic v2
id vs _id confusion · Beanie exposes .id (the str-friendly view) · match docs
